title: TxGraffiti Conjecture 15/3 resolution: a certificate-backed candidate counterexample
oneLine: A connected cubic graph on 50 vertices has minimum maximal matching number 15 but independent domination number 16, giving a bounded candidate counterexample to the stated regular-graph inequality.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate release presents a connected cubic graph G on 50 vertices with mu*(G)=15 < 16=i(G), where mu* is the minimum cardinality of a maximal matching and i(G) is the independent domination number. It also develops an exact formula-graph identity based on bilateral deficiency and a conditional order threshold for cubic graphs with a dominating induced matching. The graph and certificate are public and replayable, but the exact release has not been independently rerun, independently reimplemented, formally verified, or conventionally peer reviewed.
narration: This research release presents a certificate-backed candidate counterexample to the TxGraffiti Conjecture 15/3. The package exhibits a connected cubic graph on 50 vertices for which the minimum cardinality of a maximal matching is 15, while the independent domination number is 16, so the proposed inequality fails for this regular graph. The release also develops an exact formula-graph identity based on bilateral deficiency and a conditional order threshold for the subclass of cubic graphs with a dominating induced matching. The evidence package includes the graph in multiple encodings, explicit witnesses, a proof-tree certificate, exhaustive deterministic checks, source code, a pinned container definition, and a machine-readable claim and assurance map. All bundled theorem-critical checks pass in the recorded environment and from a clean extracted copy. It remains an unrefereed candidate: the exact release has not been independently rerun, independently reimplemented, formally verified, or conventionally peer reviewed. The graph is a public predecessor object, and the release makes no claim of first discovery, unrestricted order-50 minimality, uniqueness, or secured novelty priority. This is an Evidence Press audio briefing, released 8 August 2026. The full paper, evidence supplement, source archive and replay commands are linked on this page. The audio is an AI-generated voice summary; it is not additional mathematical evidence.

problem.name: TxGraffiti Conjecture 15/3: independent domination versus minimum maximal matching in regular graphs

keyResults: A connected cubic graph on 50 vertices satisfies mu*(G)=15<16=i(G), refuting the stated inequality for regular graphs.
An exact formula-graph identity expresses independent domination through minimum bilateral deficiency under the stated hypotheses.
Conditional on the cited 20-clause theorem, the release gives an order threshold within the subclass of cubic graphs with a dominating induced matching.
The graph, explicit witnesses, proof-tree certificate, source code and deterministic replay commands are archived together.
evidence: The DOI archive contains the manuscript and evidence supplement, the canonical graph in JSON, graph6 and edge-list encodings, explicit witnesses, a compressed proof-tree certificate, exact enumeration checks, source code, a pinned container definition, SHA-256 manifests, machine-readable claim and assurance records, provenance, sources and review-response documents. The publisher also replayed the core container on Apple silicon and the repository CI replay passes. These are scoped producer-side and publisher-side checks, not external theorem verification.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate certificate-backed result. The theorem-critical deterministic checks pass in the recorded environment, from a clean extracted copy, in the pinned core container, and in GitHub Actions. The exact release has not been independently rerun, independently reimplemented, formally verified, or conventionally peer reviewed. The release does not claim unrestricted order-50 minimality among all cubic or regular graphs, uniqueness, first discovery, or secured novelty priority. The conditional threshold theorem depends on the cited external 20-clause theorem; the public predecessor graph and exact release lineage are recorded in PROVENANCE.md.
